kinds.label: Folder
kinds.note: Microsoft lets Minerva read the whole mailbox; Minerva limits agents to the folders allowed here. Access to a folder covers its subfolders.

kinds.label: Recipient
kinds.note: Paste an address or a domain to add it. Everyone at a domain means every address there, which for a provider such as gmail.com is everyone with an account. Mail to an address can still reach others through distribution lists, aliases and forwarding.

operations.name: list_folders
operations.title: List mail folders
operations.description: List mail folders you may read: the top-level folders, or the subfolders of parent. To get the next page, repeat the call with identical arguments plus the returned next_cursor.

parent: A folder id from list_folders, or a well-known folder: inbox, sentitems, drafts, archive, deleteditems, junkemail.
List this folder's subfolders; leave out for the top-level folders.

operations.name: list_messages
operations.title: List messages
operations.description: List the messages in one folder, newest first, with a short preview of each. Filter by unread_only and received time, or search with query. To get the next page, repeat the call with identical arguments plus the returned next_cursor.

folder: A folder id from list_folders, or a well-known folder: inbox, sentitems, drafts, archive, deleteditems, junkemail.
after: Only mail received at or after this time.
before: Only mail received before this time.
query: Words to search for in this folder's mail. Results are ordered by Outlook; cannot be combined with unread_only, after or before.

operations.name: read_message
operations.title: Read a message
operations.description: Read one message as plain text, with its recipients and the names of its attachments (attachments themselves cannot be read). Long bodies are cut at max_chars; continue with offset set to the returned next_offset. Reading does not mark the message as read.

operations.name: send_message
operations.title: Send mail
operations.description: Send a new message. Every address in to, cc and bcc needs send permission. Mail is sent as plain text from the connected account and saved to Sent Items. Outlook accepts it before delivering it; a bounce arrives later as mail.

body: Plain text; sent as it is, not as HTML.

operations.name: reply
operations.title: Reply to a message
operations.description: Reply to a message you may read. The reply goes to the addresses the message asks replies to go to, or else to its sender, and each needs send permission; nobody else is copied. Mail is sent as plain text from the connected account and saved to Sent Items. Outlook accepts it before delivering it; a bounce arrives later as mail.

body: Plain text; sent as it is, not as HTML.

kinds.label: Calendar
kinds.note: Microsoft lets Minerva read every calendar of the account, including calendars others shared with it; Minerva limits agents to the calendars allowed here.

operations.name: list_calendars
operations.title: List calendars
operations.description: List the Outlook calendars you may read.

operations.name: list_events
operations.title: List events
operations.description: List the events of one calendar you may read that overlap a window of time, ordered by start, with recurring events expanded and each event in full. Without time_min or time_max, lists the next 30 days; with one of them, 30 days from or to it. The window is at most 366 days. Times are returned in UTC; all-day events have dates, the end being the day after the last day, as Microsoft reports them: for a calendar in a time zone ahead of UTC they may be a day early. To get the next page, repeat the call with identical arguments plus the returned next_cursor.

calendar_id: A calendar id from list_calendars, or "primary" for the default calendar.
time_min: Only events that end after this time.
time_max: Only events that start before this time.

operations.name: create_event
operations.title: Create an event
operations.description: Create one event in a calendar where you have create permission. The event has no attendees, so no invitations are sent, but everyone who can see the calendar can see the event. All-day events need the calendar owner's time zone.

calendar_id: A calendar id from list_calendars, or "primary" for the default calendar.
start: YYYY-MM-DD for an all-day event, or an RFC 3339 date-time with an offset.
end: Same format as start. For all-day events, the day after the last day.
time_zone: Required for all-day events, and only for them: the calendar owner's IANA time zone, like Europe/Berlin.

kinds.label: File
kinds.note: Microsoft lets Minerva open every file the account can open, in OneDrive and SharePoint; Minerva limits agents to the files, folders and libraries allowed here. Access to a folder covers everything inside it, and access to a library covers the whole library.

operations.name: list_libraries
operations.title: List libraries
operations.description: List where files live: your own OneDrive, and the document libraries of the SharePoint sites you follow (up to 25 sites). Libraries you may not read are left out; you may still have access to folders inside them, which list_folder and search_files reach. incomplete: true means you follow more sites than were listed.

operations.name: list_folder
operations.title: List a folder
operations.description: List the files and folders inside one folder or library. Use "root" for your own OneDrive. An item of type shortcut points to an item in another drive: use its target_id. Items you may not read are left out. To get the next page, repeat the call with identical arguments plus the returned next_cursor.

folder_id: A folder's or library's id from a record, or "root" for your own OneDrive.

operations.name: search_files
operations.title: Search files
operations.description: Search files and folders by words in their names and content: for work and school accounts across OneDrive, SharePoint and what was shared with you (Microsoft Search, which accepts KQL); for personal accounts in your OneDrive and what was shared with you. Only items you may read are returned, so a page may have fewer results than limit. To get the next page, repeat the call with identical arguments plus the returned next_cursor.

operations.name: get_file
operations.title: Get file details
operations.description: Read the details of one file, folder or library by id.

file_id: A file's id from a record.

operations.name: read_file
operations.title: Read a file
operations.description: Read the text of one file: Word documents and PowerPoint slides as plain text, the first sheet of an Excel workbook as CSV (stored values; dates as numbers), and text files. Other types (PDF, images, legacy .doc/.xls) are not supported. Long text is cut at max_chars and marked truncated.

file_id: A file's id from a record.

operations.name: create_file
operations.title: Create a file
operations.description: Create one text file in a folder or library where you have create permission. Use "root" for your own OneDrive. An existing file is never replaced: if the name is taken, the call fails. Everyone who can open the folder can open the file.

folder_id: A folder's or library's id from a record, or "root" for your own OneDrive.
name: The new file's name, with its extension.

kinds.label: Channel
kinds.note: Access to a team covers all its channels, including private channels the account is in and channels added later. Agents post as you. Posting to shared channels is refused.

operations.name: list_teams
operations.title: List teams
operations.description: List the Microsoft Teams teams you may read as a whole. Channels you may read in other teams are listed by list_channels.

operations.name: list_channels
operations.title: List channels
operations.description: List the channels you may read, in one team or in all the teams the account is in.

team_id: A team's id; without one, all teams.

operations.name: read_channel
operations.title: Read a channel
operations.description: Read the messages that start threads in a channel. Replies are not included; read_thread reads them. To get the next page, repeat the call with identical arguments plus the returned next_cursor. Mentions of channels and teams, links to Teams and quotes appear without their content; cards and forwarded messages are left out, and files appear by name only.

operations.name: read_thread
operations.title: Read a thread
operations.description: Read a thread in a channel: its first message (on the first page), then its replies. To get the next page, repeat the call with identical arguments plus the returned next_cursor. Mentions of channels and teams, links to Teams and quotes appear without their content; cards and forwarded messages are left out, and files appear by name only.

message_id: The id of the message that starts the thread.

operations.name: post_message
operations.title: Post to a channel
operations.description: Start a new thread in a channel where you have post permission. Text is shown literally: it cannot format, mention anyone, or link to Teams. Everyone in the channel sees it, posted as the signed-in user. Shared channels are refused.

text: Plain text, shown literally: no formatting, mentions or links to Teams.

operations.name: reply
operations.title: Reply in a thread
operations.description: Reply in a thread of a channel where you have reply permission. Text is shown literally: it cannot format, mention anyone, or link to Teams. Everyone in the channel sees it, posted as the signed-in user. Shared channels are refused.

message_id: The id of the message that starts the thread.
text: Plain text, shown literally: no formatting, mentions or links to Teams.
